summary:
India’s parliamentary commerce committee has urged stronger support for textile and apparel exporters facing US tariff uncertainty. 
It recommended faster implementation of PM MITRA, PLI and Samarth schemes, specialised MMF clusters, stronger RoDTEP and RoSCTL support, concessional export finance and US warehousing hubs. 
It also called for greater focus on sustainable textiles, carpets and handlooms.

summary:

title: Vietnam’s textile & garment exports reach to $22.8 bn in Jan-July 2026
summary:
Vietnam’s textile and garment exports, excluding yarn and fibre, inched up 1.1 per cent YoY to $22.863 billion in January-July 2026.
Yarn exports grew 11.1 per cent YoY to $2,723.846 million in value, and volume increased 3.0 per cent to 1,127,112 tonnes. 
Fabric imports reached $8.945 billion, up 2.2 per cent YoY; VITAS had set a $50 billion 2026 target for textiles, garments, and yarn.

title: AfCFTA signs $3.1-bn pact to digitise customs operations across Africa
summary:
The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Secretariat recently signed a 20-year $3.1-billion concession agreement with Bergmans Security Consultant and Supplies in Abuja to digitise customs operations across Africa.
The aim is to boost trade within Africa, reduce bottlenecks at borders and improve revenue collection.
The technology to be deployed under the pact is already successful in Nigeria.

title: US manufacturing productivity rises 1.9% in Q2 2026
summary:
US manufacturing labour productivity increased 1.9 per cent in Q2 2026, as output rose 4.6 per cent and hours worked increased 2.6 per cent, according to BLS data. 
Durable manufacturing productivity gained 2.7 per cent, while nondurable manufacturing rose 2 per cent. 
Manufacturing unit labour costs were unchanged quarter on quarter but increased 3.5 per cent YoY.

title: US Senate passes bill putting India, China at risk of 100% tariffs
summary:
The US Senate has passed a bill allowing President Donald Trump to impose tariffs of up to 100 per cent on goods from major buyers of Russian energy, including India and China. 
Passed by an 86-11 vote, the legislation now heads to the House. 
The tariffs would not be automatic, with their implementation remaining at the President's discretion.

title: Eurostat values EU's economy at $21.6 tn in 2025
summary:
Eurostat put the EU’s GDP at €18.8 trillion (~$21.6 trillion) in 2025, setting the bloc-wide economic base for market planning.
Germany led EU economies at €4.5 trillion (~$5.2 trillion), or 23.8 per cent of the total, ahead of France and Italy.
Malta had the smallest share at 0.1 per cent, behind Cyprus, Estonia and Latvia at 0.2 per cent each.

title: Australia’s apparel export declines but textiles edge up in H1 2026
summary:
Australia’s apparel imports declined 4.60 per cent to Au$12.608 billion (~$8.877 billion) in fiscal 2025–26, ABS data showed. 
Textile yarn, fabric and made-up imports edged up to Au$4.616 billion, while fibre imports rose to Au$128 million. 
Textile fibre exports surged 7.72 per cent to Au$6.473 billion, with June exports up 25.66 per cent year on year.

title: Germany's goods exports rise 0.9% in June, highest MoM gain
summary:
Germany’s adjusted goods exports rose 0.9 per cent month on month to €139.3 billion (~$160.1 billion) in June 2026, the highest monthly level recorded. 
Imports grew faster, up 4.4 per cent to €123.9 billion (~$142.4 billion), narrowing the surplus to €15.4 billion (~$17.7 billion).
EU shipments increased, while exports to the US fell, giving trade teams a mixed market picture.

title: China's foreign trade grows 19.2% YoY in July
summary:
China's yuan-denominated goods trade grew 19.2 per cent year on year in July, with exports up 17.8 per cent and imports up 21.2 per cent. 
The monthly total stayed above 4 trillion yuan (~$591.7 billion) for a fifth straight month, relevant to supply-chain planning. 
High-tech exports, including industrial robots and 3D printers, rose by over 50 per cent in July.

title: Energy, not tariffs, will decide Bangladesh’s export growth
summary:

US shipments rose 0.25 per cent to $918.74 million, and TexPro data show the market is stabilising.
A roughly 17 per cent gas-supply cut and 40-70 per cent capacity use are limiting factories despite a 10 per cent US tariff versus 12.5 per cent for Vietnam and China.

title: Can India's KKCL build on its 19% Q1 revenue growth?
summary:

EBITDA and PAT grew 29 per cent each, supported by volume expansion, a stronger brand portfolio, operational discipline and improved margins. 
The company remains confident of sustaining its growth momentum through FY27, backed by its integrated business model and continued focus on consumer demand.

title: Over 200 small Gazipur garment units declare 3-day break in Bangladesh
summary:
Over 200 small and subcontracting garment factories in Bangladesh’s Gazipur declared a three-day break beginning today as low gas pressure, combined with the coming weekend, prompted managements to extend the break. 
Large mills and factories, however, will continue to operate at full capacity today. 
However, some major manufacturers have announced three-day breaks as well.

title: Canada Goose exits Baffin ownership, sells to Royer
summary:

The deal is aimed at simplifying operations and focusing investment on Canada Goose across categories, seasons and markets.
Baffin will move to Royer as Canada Goose continues footwear and lifestyle expansion; closing is expected in August, subject to conditions.
